title: ACA s. 15 — Termination in other cases

content.overview: Section 15 governs termination of an arbitrator's mandate in circumstances other than those addressed by sections 13 and 14, including withdrawal, and provides for appointment of a substitute arbitrator.
content.glance: Section 15 governs termination of an arbitrator's mandate in circumstances other than those addressed by sections 13 and 14, including withdrawal, and provides for appointment of a substitute arbitrator.
content.study:
Module 1: Other termination routes
The provision recognises termination in circumstances identified by the Act and by withdrawal and addresses the consequences for appointment.

Module 2: Substitution
When the mandate terminates, the statutory framework requires appointment of a substitute according to the rules applicable to the original appointment, subject to express provisions.

Module 3: Prior proceedings
After substitution, the parties and tribunal must apply the statutory treatment of prior proceedings rather than assuming that every prior act is automatically repeated.

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: An arbitrator withdraws from the mandate and the substitute-appointment mechanism is engaged.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: A party asserts that the mandate ended merely because it disliked a procedural direction; the statutory termination ground must first be established.

hypotheticals.analysis: Identify the terminating event, then apply the statutory substitute-appointment rule and treatment of prior proceedings.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 15 as an automatic substitute for the surrounding statutory framework.
misconceptions.correction: Apply section 15 with its express conditions and neighbouring provisions.
